description: Solve equations involving complex unknowns: equations with z and its conjugate, systems of two linear equations in two complex unknowns, and quadratic equations with complex coefficients.

source.description: Cambodian BAC II grade-12 math textbook, Chapter 1 (complex numbers, algebraic form) — exercises only
source.extracted_by: manual OCR/transcription from scanned textbook (Claude Code), 2026-08-25

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Determine the complex number } z \text{ knowing that } (1+i)z + (3+2i)\bar z = 9+4i.
exercises.technique: Write z=x+iy, substitute, expand, and equate real and imaginary parts to solve for x and y.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Determine the real numbers } x \text{ and } y \text{ knowing that } (2+3i)x + (3-i)y = 7+5i.
exercises.technique: Expand and equate the real part and imaginary part separately to get a 2x2 real linear system in x and y.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Solve the following system of equations in the set of complex numbers:} \begin{cases} z_1+(2+i)z_2 = 4+5i \\ (1+3i)z_1+2z_2 = 2+6i \end{cases}
exercises.technique: Linear system in two complex unknowns; solve by substitution or elimination treating i as a constant satisfying i^2=-1.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Solve the following system of equations in the set of complex numbers:} \begin{cases} 2z_1-(1+i)z_2 = 6+2i \\ (2+i)z_1+iz_2 = 3+8i \end{cases}
exercises.technique: Linear system in two complex unknowns; solve by substitution or elimination treating i as a constant satisfying i^2=-1.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Solve the following equation in the set of complex numbers: } z^2+2z+5=0.
exercises.technique: Quadratic with real coefficients and negative discriminant: use the quadratic formula with the discriminant expressed via i.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Solve the following equation in the set of complex numbers: } z^2-4z+5=0.
exercises.technique: Quadratic with real coefficients and negative discriminant: use the quadratic formula with the discriminant expressed via i.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Solve the following equation in the set of complex numbers: } 2z^2-6z+5=0.
exercises.technique: Quadratic with real coefficients and negative discriminant: use the quadratic formula with the discriminant expressed via i.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Solve the following equation in the set of complex numbers: } 9z^2-6z+17=0.
exercises.technique: Quadratic with real coefficients and negative discriminant: use the quadratic formula with the discriminant expressed via i.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Determine the real numbers } p \text{ and } q \text{ knowing that } z_1=3+i \text{ is one root of the equation } z^2+pz+q=0. \text{ Then compute the other root } z_2 \text{ of the equation.}
exercises.technique: For a quadratic with real coefficients, complex roots come in conjugate pairs, so z_2=\bar z_1; use sum/product of roots (z_1+z_2=-p, z_1 z_2=q) to find p and q.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Solve the following equation in the set of complex numbers: } z^2-(4+3i)z+1+5i=0.
exercises.technique: Quadratic with complex coefficients: compute the (complex) discriminant, find its square root in the form a+bi, then apply the quadratic formula.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Solve the following equation in the set of complex numbers: } (1+i)z^2+(1-7i)z-8+6i=0.
exercises.technique: Quadratic with complex coefficients: compute the (complex) discriminant, find its square root in the form a+bi, then apply the quadratic formula.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Determine the real number } a \text{ knowing that the equation } z^2-(5+2i)z+a+4i=0 \text{ has one real root and one complex (non-real) root.}
exercises.technique: Substitute a real root z=x (x real) into the equation, separate real and imaginary parts to find x and a, then find the other root.
